title: Book 2 — Euterpe, Chapter 269
paragraphs: As regards the Oracles — both that among the Hellenes and that in Libya — the Egyptians tell the following tale. The priests of the Theban Zeus told me that two women in the service of the temple had been carried off from Thebes by Phoenicians, and that they had heard one of them had been sold into Libya and the other into Hellas; and these women, they said, were the ones who first founded the prophetic seats among the peoples I have named. When I asked how they knew so precisely of this tale they told, they replied that a great search had been made by the priests for these women, and they had not been able to find them, but they had afterwards heard this tale about them, which they were telling me.
